transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because... I keep hearing these voices at work. I'm a nursing assistant, and lately, I've been hearing voices coming from the call-light speaker and the hallway vents. They keep telling me which patient records have been changed. 

It's as clear as somebody standing right next to me, but... even when the unit is completely quiet, nobody else seems to hear it. So, that's why I came in.
How long have you been hearing these voices?
It's been going on for about two months now. It started right around the time... well, right when I was asked to help lead the wound-care documentation rollout at work.
Before the voices began, had you used any recreational drugs or misused any prescription medications?

No, nothing like that. I don't use any recreational drugs at all. And... I haven't taken any prescriptions that weren't mine, or taken extra or anything like that. Working in healthcare, I'm pretty strict about medications. So no, it's definitely not from drugs.
Have you had any new medical or neurological problems recently, such as seizures, a head injury, or another illness?

No, nothing like that. I haven't hit my head or had any seizures. My physical health has actually been completely fine... no new illnesses or anything else going on physically. It's really just the voices.
Do you believe the voices’ claims about patient records are true, even when other people disagree?

Yes, I do believe them. I know the wound-care charts are showing a pattern that management doesn't want anyone to see. My supervisor keeps telling me it's just late entries or coding mistakes, but I know that's not true. I can tell they're watching what I write in the system now, because I'm the one who caught it. The voices are just confirming what I already know.
Since the voices first began, have they been present continuously, without a period when they completely stopped?

I'm... I'm not really sure. It feels like they've just been there the whole time since this all started. I haven't exactly kept track of every single day, so if there was a time when they completely stopped, I... I didn't really notice it. They just seem to always be around.

{"intent":"Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have lasted at least one month, supporting schizophreniform disorder rather than unspecified psychosis.","question":"Have the voices and belief about the records been present for at least one full month?""}

Yes, it's been at least a month. I'd say this has all been going on for about two months now. It started right around the time I was asked to help lead the new wound-care documentation rollout at work.
Have other people noticed that your speech or thinking has become difficult to follow or unusually disorganized?

No, no one has mentioned anything like that to me. I mean, my supervisor thinks I'm wrong about the charts, but nobody has said they can't understand what I'm saying or that I'm not making sense. I feel like I'm explaining things pretty clearly.
Have the voices and belief about the records continued during times when your mood felt normal?

No, actually. I never heard those call-light voices or saw the hidden messages in the charts before all this started... before I got so driven and wound up about the new rollout. They really only started happening after I was sleeping less and working nonstop, feeling so certain that I had to fix everything at the facility. So, no, they haven't happened when I felt normal.
During that period of feeling driven and wound up, did you have an unusually elevated or irritable mood most of the day for at least one week?

Yes, definitely. It's been going on for weeks. Some days I just feel... I don't know, like I'm finally awake and I'm the one who's meant to fix everything at work. I have all this energy for it. But then, if my husband or one of the nurses tells me I need to slow down or take a break, I just snap at them. It's like they're trying to block me from doing something really important, and it just makes me so irritable.
